name: NVIDIA H200 NVL
memory_bandwidth_basis: HBM3e 5.0Gbps x 6144-bit = 4,800 GB/s (NVIDIA states 4.8TB/s for both H200 variants).
notes: AUDIT CORRECTION: the dense/sparse flag on the tensor rows was inverted. FP16 835.5 / FP8 1670.5 TFLOPS are DENSE; NVIDIA prints 1,671/3,341 'With sparsity'. These rows were previously flagged dense:false, which wrongly told a reader they were sparse.  The stored numbers are correct dense values. CRITICAL: NVIDIA prints 835 TF32 / 1,671 BF16+FP16 / 3,341 FP8+INT8 for H200 NVL, all WITH SPARITY - dense is half. H200 NVL is the air-cooled enterprise card: same 141GB HBM3e / 4.8TB/s as the SXM part, so it is a drop-in capacity upgrade for H100 NVL, at reduced Tensor throughput (835 vs 989 sparse) and a lower 600W cap. NVIDIA's spec table carries a 'preliminary specifications' footnote. MIG profiles differ from SXM: 7 MIGs @16.5GB (NVL) vs 7 @18GB (SXM). Bus width inferred. The 'other' row is FP64 30 TFLOPS (dense) - this schema's precision enum has no fp64 member.
